content.text: Plan Your Masters Trip Things to Do Food & Drink Local Tips & Guides Masters Week Blogs The Story Behind the Tournament and the City That Hosts It The Masters Tournament is one of the most iconic events in sports, and its history is deeply connected to Augusta, Georgia. From the founding of Augusta National Golf Club to the traditions that define Masters Week today, the tournament has shaped the city’s identity and global reputation. This page offers an overview of the Masters’ history and Augusta’s lasting role in the game of golf, providing context for visitors who want to better understand the legacy behind the tournament. The Origins of the Masters Tournament Augusta National Golf Club & Its Legacy Masters Traditions Visitors Should Know Augusta’s Role in Golf History Explore Masters History in Augusta The Masters Tournament was first played in 1934, following the creation of Augusta National Golf Club by legendary amateur golfer Bobby Jones and investment banker Clifford Roberts. The club’s grounds were previously a commercial nursery, a unique origin that continues to influence the course’s landscape and iconic plant life today. From its earliest days, the Masters was designed to be different, combining world-class competition with timeless traditions that continue to define the tournament. Augusta National Golf Club has become synonymous with excellence in golf. Known for its meticulously maintained course, seasonal beauty, and storied landmarks, the club plays a central role in shaping the Masters experience each year. While Augusta National itself is private and accessible only to patrons during the tournament, its presence has had a lasting impact on Augusta’s culture, economy, and global recognition as a golf destination. Part of what makes the Masters so special is its dedication to tradition. Visitors often recognize the tournament for its signature elements, including the Green Jacket, the Par 3 Contest, and the focus on sportsmanship and etiquette. These traditions help set the Masters apart and contribute to the unique atmosphere that surrounds Augusta each spring. Beyond hosting the Masters, Augusta has long been connected to the game of golf. The city is home to public and private golf courses, golf-related attractions, and year-round experiences that reflect its place in golf history. Visitors interested in learning more about Augusta’s golf heritage can explore local exhibits and attractions that showcase the city’s role in shaping the sport. The Augusta Museum of History features a dedicated golf and Masters exhibit that highlights the tournament’s evolution and Augusta’s connection to the game. This exhibit offers visitors a deeper look at memorable moments, local impact, and the stories that have shaped Masters Week over the decades.
